research_note: Selected for this session after checking primary source pages. Connections are editorial judgments, not speaker endorsements. Books, papers, and recordings were not reviewed in full; listing checks and access limits are noted below.

resources.title: Rust Atomics and Locks
resources.why: Work through memory ordering and the construction of locks and other synchronization primitives.
resources.caveat: The author provides the full book online; print and commercial ebook editions are separate.

resources.title: Rust atomic types and memory ordering
resources.why: Check the standard library's ordering guarantees and restrictions before judging an atomic pattern.

resources.title: Loom
resources.why: Explore small concurrent tests across possible thread and memory-model interleavings.
resources.caveat: Model checking applies within the tested model and bounds; it does not replace a correctness argument.

resources.title: Rust Atomics in the Wild: Memory Ordering Design Patterns from Popular Crates
resources.why: Follow the same speaker's earlier session on atomic patterns found in Rust crates.
resources.caveat: Official timetable and speaker roster checked. Detail-page access was inconsistent; delivery and recording remain unverified.

resources.title: Talking to ghosts
resources.why: Extend atomic coordination into the harder problem of reclaiming memory while other threads may still read it.
resources.caveat: Future programme entry; concurrent memory reclamation is a follow-up topic, not a repeat of the EuroRust talk.
